title: Keep each device token once while tokens rotate

blocks.text: The notification service keeps the push tokens of each user's devices in a `DeviceTokens` store. Request threads register a token when an app starts, revoke it on logout, and rotate it when the push provider renews a device's token. The sender takes a `snapshot()` for every notification. Since the store went live, some users get each notification twice, and support has a log where a renewed token shows up twice in a snapshot.

items: `register(token)`: add the token unless it is already registered, and say whether it was added;
`rotate(oldToken, newToken)`: replace the old token by the new one, only if the old one is registered and the new one isn't; when it can't, change nothing and return `false`.

blocks.text: When you're done, a token is stored once however many threads register or rotate onto it at the same moment, and a rotation that returns `false` has left the store as it was. About ten lines in total.

The list inside the store is a `Collections.synchronizedList`. The tests hand the store a list of their own through the package-private constructor, which holds a thread right after a lookup with `contains` or `indexOf`, so look tokens up with one of those.

cases.says: registering a token that is already there adds nothing and reports false
rotating a registered token replaces it; rotating an unknown one changes nothing
two threads registering the same token at once leave it stored once, even though the list inside is a synchronized list
a registration of a token that a rotation is about to write waits for the rotation, so the token is stored once
a rotation that can't happen leaves the old token registered

origin.section: A Class That Owns the State and the Lock Doesn't Depend on What It Wraps

concepts: A class that keeps the collection private and runs every read and write under its own lock makes a compound action atomic whatever the inner collection is.
